exposure: prenatal complications (prolonged rupture of membranes >24 hours, intrauterine growth restriction, preterm labour, maternal hypertension)
perinatal characteristics (gender, multiple pregnancies, gestational age, birth weight, APGAR score, intubation or ventilation in the delivery room)
neonatal complications (low weight gain during hospitalization, respiratory assistance, severe neurological anomalies, nosocomial infections)
socio-economic characteristics (socio-economic level, parental separation, urbanicity)
cohort: The study population comprised 4122 infants born prematurely at less than 35 weeks of gestation.
finding: Perinatal characteristics had the highest population-attributable fractions (around 60%) for developmental disorders, with neonatal and socio-economic determinants contributing up to 27% and prenatal complications having the lowest contributions (6-13%).
